topic: Cycle-2 frozen-prediction review of eclipse 2026-08-12 magnetic-bucket results draft rev2 (EXP-687)
proposal_verdict: REVISE (targeted) before operator approval / OTS. Rev2 is a large improvement: 11 of 13 cycle-1 holes closed, 2 partially. But 3 new or carried-over majors must be fixed first: (a) the pre-C1 H step at 16:57-17:00 UT is used as anti-dome evidence even though it coincides with the dome's own global C1 (16:59); (b) the verdict labels are still asymmetric; (c) the FSF-vs-magnetic-latitude residual test that WIN-010 publicly pre-registered is unscored. No verdict integration, no results-file commit, no OTS until cycle 3.
current_verdict_holds_note: All four predictions (PRED-095, PRED-TIER-1, PRED-TIER-3, PRED-R005) must stay our_verdict=pending. Nothing in this review changes that.

instrumentation.fallback_reason: HNOTE committed (a5749e6) after the 10:30Z dispatcher precompute; picked up on the post-audit git pull --rebase. The human note outranks the audit, so it was actioned in the same run.

our_argument_summary: Rev2 (`monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:headline`) says the magnetic bucket was non-diagnostic for both models. On the dome's named Z component the dome amplitude (-17..-21 nT) and its C1/C4 contact-phase signature are absent at all six priority stations, even though they would have been detectable. The small eclipse-shaped features that do appear are reproduced at non-eclipsed controls. B1-G-005 is scored FAILED. The core empirical case is sound: contact-phase Z amplitudes -1.7..+1.4 nT against null SDs of 0.68-2.75 nT (`monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:z_component_evaluation.per_station_Z_fits`), with injection power computed as the fraction of noise days where the fit falls below mu-3sd (`monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rework-scripts-20260927.json:scripts.zfit.py`), so the power calculation correctly accounts for null means. The remaining problems are in how the evidence is framed and labelled, plus one test that was never scored.

Label strength is still asymmetric (dome "falsified", ours "NOT CONFIRMED" for the same testable amplitude band). Carried forward as hole 1.

holes_found.description: Rev2 contradicts itself on the 16:57-17:00 UT H step and uses a dome-favourable coincidence as anti-dome evidence. control_station_check.pre_C1_step says the 3-6 nT H drop at NGK/WNG/BEL/LER/ESK at 16:57-17:00 UT came before local first contact and therefore "cannot be caused by the eclipse under either model" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:control_station_check.pre_C1_step). PRED_TIER_1.as_if then cites it as "Kp-independent" evidence against the dome, and the proposed public note says "Several stations dipped before the eclipse reached them" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:prediction_level.PRED_TIER_1). But the dome's own post_eclipse_analysis() code times its contact-phase signal to GLOBAL C1 = 16:59 UTC (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:191-195), and rev2 itself lists the 16:59 drop under dome_favourable_findings #2 (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:dome_favourable_findings). Under the dome's R3 reading, a drop at 16:57-17:00 at stations the penumbra had not yet reached is exactly what it predicts. A defender will quote our note back to us: "you admit the field dropped at 16:59, as our code said." Timing relative to LOCAL contact refutes only the local-contact reading (R2), not the global one (R3). The HER step (~1 nT, night side) is too small to count as a clean control against R3, and CTL-1 cannot in principle rule out a mechanism the dome frames as global.
holes_found.recommendation: Remove the pre-C1 step from the refutation case in PRED_TIER_1.as_if and from both proposed notes. Rewrite pre_C1_step to say: the step precedes local first contact (so it is not an obscuration-driven effect), and it coincides with the dome's global C1 (16:59). R3 is then answered on its own terms by (i) absence on Z, the dome's named component (R3 joint-fit amplitudes -1.9..+1.6 nT); (ii) H amplitude at a quarter or less of the claim; (iii) the 4.7-13% base rate for the double coincidence. Keep the 17:09 window-edge explanation for the protocol peaks, which is correct and separate.

holes_found.description: Verdict labels are still asymmetric for the same observational status. Under DR-1 the dome's -17..-21 nT range is "testable and absent" and gets recommended_verdict "falsified". Our own B1-M-001 upper band (about -25 to -12 nT eclipse-attributable, which fully contains -17..-21) is "testable and not observed at any station after CTL-1", yet it is scored "NOT CONFIRMED" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:registered_prediction_scorecard.B1-M-001.as_if vs prediction_level.PRED_095.recommended_verdict). The same data and the same amplitude band are given different words depending on whose prediction it is. This is the residue of the cycle-1 asymmetry hole the operator asked about. The rules are now symmetric; the vocabulary is not. The headline also does not say that our own falsifier OBS-O-02 fired (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:headline vs criteria.OBS_O_02).
holes_found.recommendation: Score B1-M-001 in the same terms as the dome: "as-if under DR-1: upper portion (about -12 to -25 nT) REFUTED (testable, absent); lower portion (-5 to about -10 nT) untested at this noise level". Use "refuted/falsified" or "not observed" for both, never one word for them and another for us. Add one headline clause: "one of our own pre-registered falsifiers (OBS-O-02) fired: this was not the clean test we registered."

holes_found.description: A publicly pre-registered test of ours is left unscored. The published WIN-010 text (data/wins.json id=010 detail prose, "we pre-register a sensitivity check for the post-2026-08-12 analysis... coverage-response exponent alpha in {0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5}") and the pending EXP-684 rewrite (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-684.json) commit us to two things. First, a per-station residual comparison, (observed dZ)/(baseline x coverage), against the dome FSF profile vs a magnetic-latitude profile. Second, "the evaluation will report both versions" (dome coverage vs ephemeris coverage, ephemeris labelled post-hoc). Rev2 contains no residual-profile comparison, no alpha sweep and no dual-coverage table: grep for alpha/exponent/magnetic-latitude profile returns nothing in monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json. This is not in the OTS-frozen file, so its registration is weaker, but it is on our public site in pre-event wording. Cycle-1 hole 4 ("score every registered ID") applies in spirit. A defender will say we dropped the one test EXP-684 itself admits is confounded in the dome's favour ("both confounds favour FSF").
holes_found.recommendation: Add a scored block to the results file for the WIN-010 profile test, using Z (as the prose specifies dZ) and H as a check, at the evaluable stations, under both coverage inputs and the five alpha values. Report the outcome whichever way it falls, with EXP-684's stated limits (solar elevation, magnetic-latitude convention, coverage-FSF correlation r~0.84). Label it "site-registered, not OTS-anchored". If Z residuals are near zero everywhere (as the fits suggest), the likely honest result is "non-discriminating", but it has to be stated, not skipped.

holes_found.description: The headline sigma claims depend on post-hoc choices that have no sensitivity check. (a) DR-1's 3-sigma bar was set after cycle 1 had seen the eclipse-day data (disclosed in honest_limits). For the obscuration-shaped reading, detectability is marginal at some stations: HAD tau60 null SD 4.82 means -17 nT is 3.5 sigma (power 0.84), and LER tau0 is 3.3 sigma (power 0.60). PRED_TIER_1's "4-7 sigma (obscuration-shaped)" therefore overstates the low end (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:z_component_evaluation.per_station_Z_fits.HAD, LER). (b) The contact-phase template is two Gaussians with sigma = 10 min, fixed in the code (gauss(c,sig=10.0), monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rework-scripts-20260927.json:scripts.tests.py). The dome never specified a pulse width, and no width sensitivity is shown. (c) The joint fit uses a linear trend only (zfit.py design matrix [1, t, s(t)]). Late-afternoon Sq curvature over a 3-4 h window will partly load onto the hump-shaped obscuration template. That is a likely mechanical reason the non-eclipsed ASC reproduces the negative-Z obscuration fits (-2.0 to -5.9 nT).
holes_found.recommendation: Add a compact sensitivity table: detection threshold at 2/3/5 sigma; contact-phase sigma at 3, 5, 10, 20 and 30 min; linear vs quadratic trend in the joint fit. The contact-phase conclusion (6-25 sigma) will almost certainly survive every variant, so say so explicitly. Correct the obscuration-shaped range to "about 3.5-7.6 sigma". If the quadratic trend removes the ASC and priority-station negative-Z fits, report that as the explanation rather than leaving them as unexplained "Z-down shape".

holes_found.description: Inconsistent station set for PRED-095. PRED_095.as_if restricts "stations with >80% coverage" to EBR and SPT using the dome's own (wrong) coverage table (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:prediction_level.PRED_095.as_if_DR1). control_day_calibration instead uses ephemeris obscuration (the "pred095_obsc80" set, where ESK and LER raw H land in range on the eclipse day; monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:control_day_calibration.summary). By ephemeris, EBR 1.00, SPT 0.99, HAD 0.94, CLF 0.93, ESK 0.91, LER 0.88 and NGK 0.85 all exceed 80% (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:per_station). Picking the dome's two-station reading makes the result look cherry-picked to a defender, even though the outcome does not change: Z minima at ESK -2.86 and LER -3.42 are equally far from -17.
holes_found.recommendation: Report PRED-095 under both station sets (dome-table >80% and ephemeris >80%), side by side, in both the scorecard and the proposed note.

holes_found.description: The dome's literal Tier-1 falsification clause is not met under one of the readings. "No coherent signal at >=3 stations with r > 0.5" is met under the contact-phase readings (0/6). It is NOT met under the obscuration-shaped reading: r > 0.5 at 6 of 6 priority stations on the eclipse day, against 7 of 30 control days at 3+ stations (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:control_day_calibration.summary). Rev2 discloses this inside PRED_TIER_1.as_if but builds the recommended verdict on "the dome's falsification clause is met", and the proposed note omits the obscuration-reading result. How unusual 6/6 is on control days is not reported (only the 3+ rate).
holes_found.recommendation: In the note and the scorecard, rest the as-if verdict on amplitude and contact-phase timing, and state plainly: "the dome's own r > 0.5 falsification clause is met on the contact-phase reading and not on the obscuration-shaped reading; under the latter the correlated shape is ~1/3 the claimed amplitude and appears at non-eclipsed ASC." Report the control-day frequency of 6/6 (not just 3+).

holes_found.description: B2-M-002 "Not met at 8 of 9 under any metric". Only 7 dome-cited stations are evaluable (COI has no data; GUI is excluded under DQ-1), so an "8 of 9" criterion cannot be met by construction (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:registered_prediction_scorecard.B2-M-002).
holes_found.recommendation: Say "unevaluable as registered (7 of 9 stations evaluable); among the 7, |dB|<2 nT at 0-4 depending on metric", keeping the non-discriminating note.

holes_found.description: The field name A_3sigma_detectable_nT = 3 x null_sd ignores the null mean. Power and z are correctly computed against mu (zfit.py: power = mean(fit < mu-3sd); z = (A-mu)/sd), but a reader dividing A by null_sd gets a different z than the one printed (e.g. EBR c14_global: A/sd = -1.36, printed z = -1.94).
holes_found.recommendation: Publish null_mean alongside null_sd, and define the detectable threshold as mu - 3sd (or rename the field).

holes_found.description: The B1-M-001 "high-obscuration" set of 12 includes SUA (Sun -8.5 deg at maximum) and BEL (-0.9 deg) (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:per_station). A daytime-derived Chapman-Sq range is not expected at stations where the Sun had set, so counting them either way muddies SC-1.
holes_found.recommendation: Flag stations with the Sun below the horizon at maximum and report B1-M-001 with and without them.

stronger_arguments.description: Justify the Kp override on the dome's own terms. The dome's stated operational quiet criterion is BOU stdev < 5 nT ("Eclipse magnetic signal IS real but requires quiet geomagnetic conditions (BOU stdev < 5 nT)", monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt, 2016/2017/2024 block). The dome also counts 2016-03-09, a Kp 2o slot per GFZ definitive (see WIN-010 / EXP-684 prose), as its "quietest on record" confirming eclipse. Computing BOU stdev for 2026-08-12 the same way would let us say "by the dome's own quiet test this day qualified / did not qualify". That is a stronger basis for the as-if evaluation than our DR-1 alone, and it applies to both sides.

Our own frozen file is the right tool against the dome's timestamp error, and the results file must not repeat that error. Anchoring the results file with OTS proves what the evaluation said at stamp time. It does not prove DR-1/DQ-1/CTL-1 existed before the eclipse data. Saying this explicitly in the results file demonstrates the distinction our Timestamp Error tab charges the dome with missing.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is right about two things: the raw H readings at its cited stations really were 13-19 nT below the quiet baseline (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:per_station protocol_peak_signed_dB_nT), and something did happen at 16:57-17:00 UT, close to its global C1 (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:control_station_check.pre_C1_step). The Kp<2 precondition is also a reasonable instinct (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:conditions.preregistered_kp_lt_2_met).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Ordinary days give the same raw H numbers (control_day_calibration). The dome's named Z component shows nothing within a factor of ~2-4 of -17 nT under any reading (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:z_component_evaluation). The 16:59 H coincidence is 2-6 nT, absent on Z, and occurs at a 4.7-13% base rate (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260927T074653.json:dome_favourable_findings). These arguments stand on their own; they do not need the misframed "dipped before the eclipse" point (hole C2-1), and using it weakens them.

decision_1_verdict_label.recommendation: Use our_verdict = "falsified" (a schema value; "falsified-with-override" is NOT in the DATA-SCHEMAS enum, so the override belongs in the note) for BOTH PRED-095 and PRED-TIER-1. Condition: C2-1, C2-2 and C2-4 must be fixed first. Do NOT use standard_physics.
reasons: For: the Kp gate is a proxy for noise, and DR-1 measures that noise directly on comparable (Kp<=3) days. The contact-phase Z signature would have been 6-25 sigma, and that survives any reasonable threshold. Kp 2.333 also falls in the dome's own unspecified 2-3 gap (not its "Kp>=3 buried" clause), and the dome accepted a Kp-2o day (2016) as confirmation. A void-by-precondition verdict would reward the escape clause this review has criticised.

Against, and why it is manageable: labelling a prediction "falsified" when its registered precondition failed is exactly what the cycle-1 asymmetry hole warned about. It stays symmetric only if our B1-M-001 upper band gets the same word under the same override (C2-2). If the operator is unwilling to apply "refuted" to our own upper band, the consistent fallback is to keep both PRED-095/TIER-1 at "pending", with a "precondition unmet; claimed signal absent at detectable amplitude" note. It is not a split label.

standard_physics is the wrong category. It asserts that the dome prediction restates standard physics, but the kappa-scaled -17..-21 nT amplitude and the C1/C4 contact-phase timing are dome-specific claims with no standard-physics basis. Only the "Z minimum near max coverage" timing clause of PRED-095 is standard-compatible, and that clause alone is not the prediction.

decision_2_post_hoc_rules_in_results_fil.recommendation: YES, include DR-1, DQ-1, CTL-1, the joint fit and the control-station set in the OTS-anchored RESULTS file, with explicit labelling. They are needed to reproduce the verdicts, and omitting them would hide the analysis choices.
conditions: Each rule object carries machine-readable fields: preregistered:false, defined_at (ISO), defined_in_response_to (cycle-1 review path). Currently only honest_limits prose says this, and the symmetric_evaluation_rules block has no per-rule flag.
Keep these rules in a block physically separate from the scoring of pre-registered criteria, and never re-word frozen criteria inside it.
The _meta must state that the OTS stamp anchors the evaluation content at stamp time and does not establish that any post-hoc rule predates the eclipse data (see stronger_arguments #2).
The frozen predictions file is untouched regardless. The Kim & Chang (ISS-3101) fix goes in a separate dated erratum file, which rev2 correctly does not attempt.

other_focus_checks.injection_recovery: Spot-checked from monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rework-scripts-20260927.json:scripts.zfit.py. Injection adds -17 x template to each real control-day deviation (Kp<=3 in 12-24 UT), refits the same template, and counts fits below mu-3sd. The method is sound, and the injection shape equals the dome's claimed shape under each reading. It does not test shape mismatch (pulse width, trend curvature), hence C2-4. The DR-1 threshold was set after the eclipse-day data had been seen; this cannot be verified from artifacts and is disclosed in honest_limits.
other_focus_checks.symmetry: Rules are symmetric (SR-1, DR-1, DQ-1, CTL-1 are applied to both sides); the labels are not (C2-2).
other_focus_checks.own_misses_disclosed: OBS-D-02 non-diagnostic (SC-5, criteria) - yes. B1-M-001 17/30 (SC-5, scorecard) - yes. OBS-O-02 FIRED (criteria) - yes, but not in the headline (C2-2). B1-G-005 FAILED - yes, and in the headline.
other_focus_checks.HER_correction: Verified as plausible: Hermanus (34.4S, 19.2E) sunset in mid-August is roughly 15:55-16:10 UT, so night side after ~16:15 UT is right. The cycle-1 "dayside" description was wrong. HER is a valid control for external/global features, but a weak control for dayside Sq curvature; ASC/KOU cover that.
other_focus_checks.kim_chang: Rev2 does not edit the frozen file and flags ISS-3101 in honest_limits. Correct.
other_focus_checks.public_date_2026_10_15: Not hard-coded in rev2 (grep for 2026-10-15 returns nothing). It IS hard-coded in the pending EXP-684 WIN-010 prose ("the target for publishing the reviewed evaluation... is 2026-10-15"). With a cycle-3 revision now needed (analyst rework, then curmudgeon cycle 3, then operator approval, then OTS), 18 days under a hand-fired pipeline is feasible but tight. The operator should confirm or move the date before EXP-684 publishes.

recommended_action_note: Targeted revision, not a rewrite. C2-1 and C2-2 are wording/label changes; C2-3 is one new scored block; C2-4 is a sensitivity table. Cycle 3 should be class deep-attack scoped to C2-3 (new analysis content) plus verification of C2-1/2/4-9.
deeper_analysis: The other side, argued as a dome defender: (1) "Kp was 2.333; by your own SR-1 the test is void, so any falsified label is you overriding my precondition while protecting your own range with the detectability rule." Answer: DR-1 treats both sides the same way, and our range survives only in its lower half, which is undetectable. That defence holds only if our upper half is called refuted in the same words (C2-2). (2) "The field dropped at 16:59, my global C1, at stations your eclipse had not reached. You say so yourself." This is the defender's best line against rev2 as written. It is answered by Z absence and the base rate, not by local-contact timing (C2-1). (3) "My signal is global and aetheric, so your non-eclipsed controls are not controls." That makes the claim unfalsifiable by station comparison, but it does not rescue the amplitude, which is absent on the named component everywhere. (4) "You skipped the FSF profile test you advertised." That is fair until C2-3 is fixed. Overall: the empirical core of rev2 (Z amplitudes and contact-phase absence with measured power) is robust, and I expect it to survive cycle 3; the fixes are presentation and completeness.

summary_for_decider: Cycle 2 on EXP-687 rev2: REVISE (targeted). 11/13 cycle-1 holes closed, 2 partial. New: C2-1 (major) pre-C1 16:57-17:00 H step coincides with the dome's global C1 16:59 and must not be used as anti-dome evidence; C2-2 (major, carry-over ISS-3088) label asymmetry: dome "falsified" vs our same-band "not confirmed"; C2-3 (major) the WIN-010 site-pre-registered FSF-vs-magnetic-latitude residual + alpha sweep + dual-coverage test is unscored. Moderates: sigma/width/trend sensitivity, PRED-095 station set, Tier-1 r>0.5 clause met on the obscuration reading. Keep all four predictions pending; do not commit the results file; do not OTS. Route back to analyst (EXP-687 continuation); the next curmudgeon pass is cycle 3, deep-attack scoped to C2-3. Operator decisions: see operator_decisions (falsified for both only with symmetric labels, otherwise pending for both; never standard_physics; post-hoc rules included in the results file with preregistered:false flags). Also confirm or move the 2026-10-15 public date in EXP-684.
content_security: No prompt-injection content found in reviewed artifacts.
